title: What the mound's smell does about it
question: Both these colonies breed at the same high drift. In one, the mound they stand on pulls them back to one smell. Which one, and is it the better box?
context_md:
**The second mechanism, on its own.** Newborns drift at the same high setting in BOTH panels, so that is not the difference. The only difference is whether the mound carries a smell that an ant standing on it takes a little of and leaves a little of its own into.

This is what ships turned on, though at a much gentler drift than either of these.

**What the numbers say, and it cuts both ways.** The blending does what it was built to do: killings of its own family fall from 675 to 181. But the colony that stops eating itself is much smaller, 32 against 155 - because on this bed 675 killings are also 675 meals, and a colony that cannot feed itself was living off its own dead. That is a bed problem rather than a smell problem, and it is worth your eye on it.

**Your question about what happens to an ant that drifts too far:** it is treated as a stranger by everyone at home, so it has no colony and it founds none. A new colony only arrives with budding - a party walking out of a crowded nest to found a second mound - which is the next build, not this one.

**And on "too long away turns him enemy":** that shape is not in this build, and I would rather say so than let the card imply it. An ant's smell moves when it is BORN, not while it is away; coming home is what undoes it. An ant that never comes home simply keeps the smell it was born with. Making time-away itself the thing that turns an ant into a stranger is a small change to the same machinery, and I can build it if you want that shape.

The HUD says PAUSED because the harness ticks the box directly; it is genuinely running.

items.label: A - no smell in the mound
items.caption: drift 1.0, blending off

items.label: B - the mound holds a smell
items.caption: drift 1.0, blending on
